use_cases.name: Reactive Updates on Input Changes
use_cases.preconditions: A permitted recommendation or shot page with editable inputs.
use_cases.postconditions: The visible result always belongs to the displayed input snapshot.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-643/644. ShotResultRequest/useShotResult guard shot pages; QuickCallRequest/useQuickCallResult guard QuickCall. This documents Gurk’s integration guard only; SCRUM-628 QuickCall functionality remains Abdul’s work.

steps_and_alternatives.text: User changes a result-defining input or selects a preset scenario.
Immediately hide the old result and related download actions, and cancel or invalidate the previous request before the debounce completes.
After the debounce or explicit Run action, capture the inputs and request the corresponding result.
User changes inputs again before the prior request returns.
UI cancels/ignores the stale response.
UI uses only the latest request.
Use case resumes at step 4.
Accept a completion only if it belongs to the latest active request. Store its successful input snapshot with the result.
Update request fails.
UI clears the failed result and hides its export action; it does not keep an old ranking under changed controls.

use_cases.name: Review Shot-Plan Recommendations
use_cases.preconditions: Signed-in analyst or coach; validated derived shot data; valid distinct teams.
use_cases.postconditions: A current complete plan or an explicit unavailable/error state is visible.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-544/642/643. Rankings blend our season-wide offense with opponent season-wide defense and league shrinkage. They are not head-to-head-only results, possession PPP, causal defensive weaknesses or individual future-shot guarantees.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Analyst or coach opens Shot Plan and selects season, two different teams, k and offense weight; heatmap filters and cap are selected separately.
Capture one input set and request season-wide shot-type/zone rankings plus the selected matchup heatmap. Show the plan only after both succeed.
Required shot aggregates or the requested heatmap cannot load.
Keep the incomplete Shot Plan hidden and display its request error.
Other working play-type pages remain available; their results are independent of this failed shot request.
Use case ends.
Play-by-play data for this matchup is sparse.
Show the actual sample counts and sample-size shrinkage; do not invent a confidence score.
Disclose sample sizes and league shrinkage; do not invent a confidence interval.
Interpret the current plan using the displayed counts and limitations.
Display estimated points per shot attempt, adjusted offense/defense rates and sample sizes. Explain that heatmap type/zone filters do not alter the season-wide rankings.
Show the attempt-count heatmap with matching, plotted, invalid-location, outside-half-court and cap-omitted counts.
Export PDF through the authenticated same-origin route using the successful filters and cap. The PDF recomputes from current loaded sources and records those versions.

use_cases.name: Evaluate Next-Season PPP (offline)
use_cases.preconditions: At least four usable regular seasons with prior-season coverage; Python evaluation environment.
use_cases.postconditions: Versioned offline evidence files exist; no live forecast endpoint is added.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-526. Analyst runs the offline evaluation script with the retained Synergy CSV. Preconditions: at least four regular seasons with usable immediately preceding-season rows. The script builds lagged features, tunes Ridge on the penultimate target season, refits earlier targets, scores the final season once, compares two prior-season baselines, then saves report.json and predictions.csv. Missing training/tuning/final coverage raises ValueError. Outcomes are a historical season-ahead backtest, not a live app or pre-game forecast. No deployment or extra API endpoint is implied.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Analyst runs run_forecast_evaluation.py with a retained Synergy CSV and an output directory.
Build target rows using only the immediately preceding regular season as features; count excluded rows without that coverage.
Train on earlier target seasons and tune Ridge alpha on the penultimate target season; fit scaling within each training fit.
Refit the selected pipeline using targets earlier than the final season, then score the final target season once.
Compare MAE, RMSE and signed bias with prior-team and prior-league baselines; report bins and coverage.
Save report.json and predictions.csv with source and prediction hashes. Describe the result as a historical season-ahead backtest.
If training, tuning or final prior-season coverage is missing, stop with ValueError; do not substitute same-season predictors.

use_cases.name: Versioned CSV Tables
use_cases.preconditions: A readable versioned source and access permitted for the requested feature.
use_cases.postconditions: Each result/export identifies its actual input bytes; no unrelated disk hash is substituted.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-487. A content version establishes identity, not data correctness or prediction accuracy.

steps_and_alternatives.text: System loads a CSV or Parquet source while capturing its SHA-256; reject a file that changes during the read.
Associate the version with the returned DataFrame and carry that loaded version through API results and supported response headers.
User can inspect the active version in source details and exported data. The current UI has no historical version selector.
Shared report exports keep the displayed result version. Specialized shot CSV/PDF exports identify the source used when the file is generated.
Displayed source version no longer matches a guarded download.
Reject the guarded download with409 and keep its error visible; do not offer a historical version selector.
User reloads the current result before requesting that download again.
Heatmap PNG and saved-metrics CSV compare the expected displayed version and reject a changed source with 409.

use_cases.name: Short Explanations per item
use_cases.preconditions: A successful current ranking.
use_cases.postconditions: Each explanation describes its actual result and model scope.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Coach opens a successful baseline or context ranking.
Show a short evidence-based explanation for each ranked play type using the metrics returned with that result.
Gap is near zero / ambiguous.
System selects a neutral template rather than overstating an advantage.
Display the explanation with the actual baseline or context scope.
For baseline results, state that season aggregates are used and score, period, clock and coaching conditions do not change the ranking.
For context results, identify applied conditions and disclose inputs that were only retained as notes.
Keep missing statistics unavailable and avoid unsupported causal claims, invented confidence intervals or guarantees.

use_cases.name: Compute & Export Top-K Uplift (CSV/JSON)
use_cases.preconditions: Signed-in analyst; valid filters and readable source data.
use_cases.postconditions: A versioned historical comparison or a clear request/data error is returned.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-475. Historical modeled Top-K comparison, not causal or held-out performance. Team baseline uses SUM(PTS)/SUM(POSS) over all team-season offensive rows. Selected modeled PPP uses SUM(PPP_PRED*POSS_OFF)/SUM(POSS_OFF). JSON and CSV contain scope, numerators, denominators, K, units, formulas, source SHA-256 and row contributions. Missing PTS fails explicitly; zero baseline gives null relative uplift. SCRUM-474 remains a separate evaluation dependency. Analyst selects season, teams, K and offense weight, then reads or downloads equivalent JSON/CSV evidence. Invalid filters 400/422; no eligible observations 404. Authorization failures 401/403.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Analyst selects a retained season, our team, opponent, K and offense weight for the historical matchup comparison.
System loads the season-level modeled ranking and the observed source aggregates, with possession-weighted team/play-type rows.
Compare the weighted modeled Top-K value with the weighted seasonal comparison and return the numerator, denominator, requested K and actual K.
No eligible source observations or an unusable comparison denominator.
Return a clear data error for missing required values; a zero baseline yields null relative uplift.
Keep scope and available sample counts explicit; do not invent a confidence score.
Return JSON or CSV with units and actual source versions so the weighted comparison can be reproduced.
Describe the result as historical modeled uplift. It is not a held-out forecast, causal treatment effect or a promise that choosing a play will improve scoring.
Export fails.
System shows an error.
System allows the Analyst to retry.
Retry the same valid export request or correct the filters before retrying.
Return JSON or CSV with requested/actual K, weighted numerators, seasonal comparison, units and source version.
Describe modeled Top-K uplift as retrospective evidence, not causal gain or a guarantee from changing play choice.

use_cases.name: Explore Shot Attempts and Heatmaps
use_cases.preconditions: Analyst for shot rows/CSV; analyst or coach for heatmap; valid filters.
use_cases.postconditions: Current results are labeled with their actual filters and source; valid downloads contain no credentials.
use_cases.scope: Analysts browse shot attempts and export CSV. Analysts and coaches render matchup heatmaps and download PNG. Counts describe attempts, not accuracy or defensive weakness. SCRUM-643.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Analyst opens Shot Explorer, or analyst/coach opens Shot Heatmap, and selects the permitted season/team/opponent/type/zone filters.
Submit the captured inputs. Clear old table/image/download controls while loading; input changes or failure never relabel an older result.
Explorer shows matching and returned row counts. CSV uses the same filters with the documented export cap and identifies the current canonical source.
Heatmap excludes invalid locations and shots outside the physical half court, then applies deterministic sampling only above the selected cap.
Display a linear attempt-count scale for makes and misses together. Matching attempts equal plotted plus each exclusion and cap omission.

Download PNG through the same-origin proxy with the displayed filters, cap and source version. Verify current role, fixed upstream, echoed inputs/counts/version and PNG signature before returning a private attachment.
No matches returns a clear no-data message. Matches with no usable half-court locations retain exclusion counts.
Reject unauthorized requests and malformed inputs. PNG version mismatch returns409; mismatched/invalid upstream image returns502. Errors are not attachments.

use_cases.name: Review Saved Shot-Model Evidence
use_cases.preconditions: Signed-in analyst; saved artifacts matching the current cleaned-shot source.
use_cases.postconditions: Saved evidence is shown with limitations, or a clear unavailable/retry state without stale metrics.

Load the saved five-fold artifact and verify result kind, artifact version, source hash and fold count. Do not fit a model during the HTTP request.
Show training-game cross-validation separately from the untouched later-season diagnostic, with the sample definition and model comparison.

Missing, stale, corrupt or mismatched artifacts return503 and require a new offline evaluation. Reload only retries reading.
refresh=true returns400 and never trains on the server. Unknown numerical values display Unavailable; absent results disable export.

use_cases.name: Save Notes to Tactics Board / Plan
use_cases.preconditions: Authenticated coach; a valid distinct-team matchup; reads and writes use the owning user ID.
use_cases.postconditions: Only the owner coach can access the state. The matchup identity and audit fields remain immutable to clients; accepted updates advance the revision.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-481 covers the persisted schema contract only. Coach UI migration and synchronization are separate SCRUM-482/483 work. This collaboration reuses the existing Gameplan Storage structural design. The database does not itself emit an HTTP409 conflict: a conditional update can affect zero rows, which the caller must detect and resolve.

steps_and_alternatives.text: An authenticated coach prepares notes, plan and role values for one season and directed matchup. This flow specifies the storage contract, not completion of the separate UI integration.
For new state, INSERT the composite key and allowed state fields. Row-level security requires auth.uid() ownership and the current protected profile role coach; constraints validate the payload.
For existing state, read its revision and UPDATE only notes, plan and roles using the full owner/matchup key and revision = last_read_revision. Do not use an unconditional upsert.
No persisted owner/matchup row exists.
The authorized caller INSERTs a new row with allowed state fields; defaults initialize revision and audit timestamps.
Validate payload and coach ownership before accepting the inserted state.
On duplicate key, reload the existing row and use the conditional-update path instead of upsert.
Write fails or no conditional update row is returned.
Do not confirm a successful save after a denied, invalid or failed write.
The caller retains its unsaved edit until it can reload and reconcile with the authorized current revision.
Retry only after resolving the error and reading the revision used for a conditional update.
On a successful update, the database increments revision and updated_at. The caller accepts the returned state and revision only after confirming a row was written.
Anonymous, analyst, pending and other-coach sessions cannot read or change this owner state. Authorization uses the protected profile role, not editable signup metadata.
If a conditional update writes zero rows, do not report a successful save. Reload the authorized current state and reconcile changes before retrying against its new revision.
A duplicate INSERT is a conflict; read the existing owner/matchup row before an explicitly conditional update. Changing owner, season or team keys requires a distinct new record, not an UPDATE.
Reject invalid JSON shape, more than50 plan entries, more than100 notes, duplicate plan IDs or state above65536bytes. SQL constraints also require valid team/season formats and different teams.
Deleting an auth user removes its owned rows through the existing foreign key. No test here claims teammate client-sync behavior or an end-user recovery workflow.

use_cases.preconditions: Signed-in approved analyst.

Authentication fails.
System halts the flow.
System redirects to sign-in.
Use case ends in failure.

Reload the page data after the source becomes available.

System flags the specific issue.

use_cases.name: Load PBP Parquet
use_cases.preconditions: Documented raw provider inputs and local rebuild environment; no public upload interface is implied.
use_cases.postconditions: Validated derived files and provenance exist; excluded or unknown records remain disclosed.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-538/549/642. Current retained release has six seasons. Quarantine/count totals belong to versioned evidence, not immutable requirements. No claim of perfect provider coordinates or future forecast accuracy.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Maintainer acquires pinned official provider play-by-play files for the documented seasons and records URLs, pull time and raw hashes outside the public source package.
Offline rebuild validates unique events, game participants and score continuity. Quarantine inconsistent games with an exclusion manifest; preserve raw input.
File missing or unreadable.
Rebuild reports the unreadable source file and stops before replacing validated artifacts.
Use case resumes at step 1.
Derive the shooting team, opponent, pre-shot margin, shot outcome and known attempt value from explicit event evidence. Unknown missed-shot values remain missing.
Schema mismatch.
System flags the mismatch.
System blocks downstream use until resolved.
Use case ends in failure.

Normalize provider shot types and basket-relative locations. Apply official court boundaries, known two/three-point evidence and explicit geometry-only fallback; flag implausible locations rather than invent coordinates.
Rebuild cleaned/canonical shots, team/opponent aggregates and league rates. Invalid spatial locations are excluded from charts/spatial models; unknown zones are excluded from zone rankings.
Validate retained events and aggregate counts against pinned raw input. Write source sidecars and hashes, then regenerate saved diagnostics offline before deploying derived files.

use_cases.name: Run Data Quality Checks
use_cases.preconditions: Signed-in analyst; configured Synergy source.
use_cases.postconditions: Current source status or a clear retry error is visible.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-480. Source data checks; scoped to the Synergy input. SCRUM-640 keeps technical details optional without hiding limitations.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Analyst opens Data Explorer or selects Retry data checks. The previous report is cleared while checks load.
The API verifies the analyst role and checks required columns, missing keys, duplicate rows and expected team-season coverage against one loaded Synergy source.
The response identifies the checked source and generation time; each check is pass, fail or not run with a reason.
The panel shows the source-wide status independently of the preview filters. These checks do not measure model accuracy or validate shot data.
One or more checks fail.
System clearly flags which check failed and why.
System reports safe_for_use=false for failed source checks; it does not silently relabel the source as safe.
Use case resumes at step 5.
A check cannot be run (e.g., a reference table is missing).
System marks that check as not run and states the reason in the report.
Use case resumes at step 5.
Analyst can expand check details or retry. A failed, timed-out or superseded request never displays a previous pass as current.

use_cases.postconditions: The exported bounded snapshot matches its displayed rows and applied filters.

Displayed snapshot is empty, stale or missing required fields.
System rejects missing or invalid snapshot fields with a clear error; no partial report is presented as complete.
Refresh the page result and retry export only once it is valid and current.

use_cases.preconditions: Signed-in analyst and matching prepared model/evaluation inputs.

Request current diagnostics independently from metadata requests. Regular metric routes may compute and cache evaluations; display each loading, error and ready state separately.
Show earlier-season training diagnostics separately from the later-season evaluation; use the exact displayed table for shared metric reports.
The diagnostic sample has different coverage or observed-season feature scope.
Show sample coverage and retrospective limitations beside the metrics.
Interpret the current result with those limitations; no future-accuracy claim is added.
Calibration groups predicted and realized PPP into bins and reports bias, MAE, RMSE, sample counts and source provenance.
Keep the limitation visible: observed-season rate features make these retrospective diagnostics, not pre-game or future-season predictions.
Show predicted-versus-realized PPP bins, signed bias, MAE and RMSE for later-season diagnostic folds.
Disclose that contemporaneous observed-season features make this a retrospective diagnostic; it does not establish future or pre-game accuracy.
Keep metadata, metrics and calibration request states separate so a successful metadata response cannot leave the metrics page stuck loading.

use_cases.name: Data Dictionary

use_cases.postconditions: Actual fields and documented meanings are visible, including explicit unknown definitions.

The API lists actual dataset columns with meaning, units and source.

use_cases.name: Audit Metadata
use_cases.preconditions: Authenticated session; Data Explorer itself requires analyst access.
use_cases.postconditions: Current source metadata or a clear unavailable state is visible.
use_cases.scope: SCRUM-488/489. Source row counts are input-file counts, not filtered preview counts; the catalog covers Synergy, ML predictions, cleaned/canonical shots and two aggregate datasets.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Analyst opens Data Explorer and the source panel requests the authenticated dataset catalog.
System returns active dataset IDs, availability, actual source row counts and season coverage from the loaded files.
Metadata is missing for a dataset.
System shows "audit metadata unavailable" rather than omitting the panel silently.
Show Not recorded for a missing pull date or Retry for a failed catalog request.
The source panel shows the play-type source summary. Expanding Source details reveals the SHA-256 version and recorded pull date.
If a pull date is not recorded, display Not recorded; file modification time must not be substituted.
On failure, show an error and Retry. Retry clears the previous catalog while loading; unavailable optional datasets do not invalidate other usable entries.

use_cases.postconditions: The user can identify the action, result and relevant limitation without expanding technical details.

Loading, unavailable, no-data and error states provide an appropriate next action; missing values display Unavailable rather than a misleading zero.
Do not offer unsupported controls, such as changing folds or training via the saved shot-metrics page.

use_cases.name: Ranked List via API (Baseline)
use_cases.preconditions: An approved coach is signed in and selects a season, team and different opponent.
use_cases.postconditions: Show the complete baseline ranking with source version and its season-only scope, or a clear validation/unavailable error; no partial ranking is presented.
use_cases.scope: Season-level play-type rankings use the selected matchup and offense weighting. Game score, clock and period do not change this baseline. Bounded timing checks are recorded separately and are not a guaranteed service-level agreement.

steps_and_alternatives.text: Client calls the baseline ranking endpoint with season/team/opponent/filters.
System validates the request parameters.
Invalid/missing parameters.
System returns a structured validation error.
Use case ends in failure.
System computes or retrieves cached baseline rankings.
The request is still waiting for the complete baseline ranking.
